expected.insightNarrative:
Airlines Page is the airline page of the Airline Alliance Activity Dashboard, which follows the activity of the AeroLink alliance of four airlines from 2022 to 2025. One airline is chosen in the navigation on the left, along with the year, the month and the region; the dashboard shows SkyConnect Air for July 2023 in North America. A summary strip sits at the top, and three columns of monthly KPI cards follow, for passenger traffic, cargo traffic and cost and revenue. Each card gives the month's value, its change against the previous month, a bar chart of the twelve months of the year with a dot under each month marking whether it beat the same month of the prior year, and the current month highlighted.

Key insights
- SkyConnect Air completed 1,410 flights in the month, up 1.7% on the previous month, with on-time performance of 83.6% (up 2.9%), an average distance of 5,396.79 km (down 3.1%) and an average CSAT score of 7.9 (down 0.1%). Its hub is New York (JFK) and its major route Zurich to Tokyo (ZUR-NRT).
- Passenger traffic is at its highest levels of the year: 339,851 passengers in the selected month and up to 349,145 in December, revenue passenger kilometres of 1.78B in the month and up to 1.85B in June, and a passenger load factor of 90.38% in the month, peaking at 91.24% in June.
- Cargo peaks in the last quarter: freight tonnes reach 9,331 in December, 8,924 in November and 8,740 in October; cargo tonne kilometres 49.76M, 48.93M and 47.92M in the same months; and the cargo load factor is highest in November at 77.95%, with December at 77.56% and October at 77.54%.
- Revenue is high but profit is negative: total revenue reaches $601.19M in June and $581.76M in August, with $566.79M in the selected month and $564.49M in December, while operating profit is at its lowest in November at -$176.69M and October at -$171.22M.

Airline Summary 1, Airline Summary 2
The summary strip: 1,410 completed flights (up 1.7% versus the previous month), an average distance covered of 5,396.79 km (down 3.1%), on-time performance of 83.6% (up 2.9%), the airline hub at New York, United States (JFK), the major flight route Zurich, Switzerland to Tokyo, Japan (ZUR-NRT), and an average CSAT score of 7.9 (down 0.1%).

Passenger Count BAN, Pass Count Bars, Pass Count Circles, Pass Count Labels
All passengers for the month: 339,851, up 0.7% versus the previous month, with every month of the year above the prior year.

RPK Airlines BAN, RPK Airlines Bars, RPK Airlines Circles, RPK Airlines Labels
Revenue passenger kilometres: 1.78 billion km, down 3.8% versus the previous month.

Load Factor BAN, Load Factor Bars, Load Factor Circles, Load Factor Airlines Labels
Passenger load factor: 90.4%, down 0.9% versus the previous month.

Freight Tonnes BAN, Freight Tonnes Bars, Freight Tonnes Circles, Freight Tonnes Labels
Freight carried: 7,388 tonnes, up 1.3% versus the previous month.

CTK BAN, CTK Bars, CTK Circles, CTK Labels
Cargo tonne kilometres: 39.20 million km, down 4.3% versus the previous month.

CLF BAN, CLF Bars, CLF Circles, CLF Labels
Cargo load factor: 64.9%, down 0.5% versus the previous month.

Total Revenue BAN, Total Revenue Bars, Total Revenue Circles, Total Revenue Labels
Total revenue: $566.79M, down 5.7% versus the previous month.

Op Profit BAN, Op Profit Bars, Op Profit Circles, Op Profit Labels
Total operating profit: -$10.56M, down 193.4% versus the previous month; the bars for the summer months hang below zero and the last months of the year are marked in blue as losses against the prior year.

Cost BAN, Cost Bars, Cost Circles, Cost Labels
Total operating cost: $577.35M, down 2.1% versus the previous month; the dots under the months are red for costs that exceed the prior year's.

Years, Months, Selected Region, Airline Navigation, Logged in
The dashboard's controls: the year and month buttons, the region drop-down, the navigation menu with the alliance's four airlines, and the login greeting. They carry no measures of their own.

Alliance Page is the home page of the Airline Alliance Activity Dashboard, which follows the activity of the AeroLink alliance of four airlines (Atlantic Express, Global Star, Pacific Wings and SkyConnect Airways) from 2022 to 2025. The year, month and region are selected on the left; the dashboard shows July 2023 for North America. Each KPI card gives the month's value, its change against the previous month, a bar chart of the twelve months of the year with a dot under each month marking whether it beat the same month of the prior year, and a breakdown by airline.

Key insights
- SkyConnect Airways is by far the largest carrier: 1,307 completed flights in the current month and 1,283 in the previous month, far ahead of the other members, with revenue passenger kilometres of 1.78B this month and 1.85B the month before.
- On-time performance for the alliance is 84.4% in the selected month, among the year's highest with 84.5% in March, while April, February and August are the low months at 82.0%, 82.3% and 82.6%. Global Star is the most punctual airline at 94.4% and Pacific Wings the least at 77.3%; SkyConnect Airways' previous-month rate of 82.5% was also low.
- Alliance revenue passenger kilometres were lowest in February at 1.74B. The average CSAT score is 7.9 in the selected month, a high for the year, with February the low at 7.8; Pacific Wings has the lowest CSAT at 7.8 and Atlantic Express scored 7.9 in the previous month.
- New York is the top destination with 278 completed flights this month.
- Among aircraft, the B787 has the highest load factor at 91.1% while the A330 has the lowest at 89.6%; the B777 carried the most passengers in the previous month, 100,328, and the B787 flew the fewest flights that month, 275.
- Baggage mishandling is high at Atlantic Express (91.5% in the previous month) and Pacific Wings (86.7% this month).

Comp Flights BAN, Comp Flights Bars, Comp Flights Circles, Comp Flights Labels, Comp Flights Airlines
Completed flights for the month are 1,688, up 0.7% versus the previous month. SkyConnect Airways completed by far the most flights at 1,307, ahead of Atlantic Express (188), Pacific Wings (105) and Global Star (88).

On-time performance is 84.4%, up 2.3% versus the previous month. Global Star leads at 94.4%, followed by Atlantic Express (84.5%), SkyConnect Airways (84.3%) and Pacific Wings (77.3%).

RPK BAN, RPK Bars, RPK Circles, RPK Labels, RPK Airlines
Revenue passenger kilometres are 2.38 billion km, down 3.8% versus the previous month. SkyConnect Airways accounts for most of them at 1.78 billion km, followed by Global Star (0.32 billion), Atlantic Express (0.22 billion) and Pacific Wings (0.06 billion).

The average satisfaction score is 7.9, down 0.2% versus the previous month. Global Star, Atlantic Express and SkyConnect Airways all score 7.9 and Pacific Wings 7.8.

Top Destinations
The top flight destinations in North America: New York with 278 flights, then Toronto (69), Vancouver (58), Boston (56) and Chicago (46).

Main Flight Times
A heat map of flights by month and day of the week; the darkest cells are the busiest, and the labelled low and high are 201 and 333 flights.

Aircraft Utilization
Completed flights and average load factor by aircraft type, each compared with the previous month: the B787 flew the most (317 flights) with the highest load factor (91.1%), followed by the B777 (315 flights, 90.7%), the A330 (293, 89.6%), the B737 (289, 90.3%), the A320 (281, 90.0%) and the A350 (280, 90.4%).

Mishandling, Baggage Airlines
The flights-with-baggage-mishandling indicator stands at 78.7% overall; by airline it is 86.7% for Pacific Wings, 83.5% for Atlantic Express, 79.5% for Global Star and 77.3% for SkyConnect Airways.

expected.insightNarrative:
Alliance Page is the home page of the Airline Alliance Activity Dashboard, which follows the activity of the AeroLink alliance of four airlines (Atlantic Express, Global Star, Pacific Wings and SkyConnect Airways) from 2022 to 2025. The year, month and region are selected on the left; the dashboard shows July 2023 for North America. Each KPI card gives the month's value, its change against the previous month, a bar chart of the twelve months of the year with a dot under each month marking whether it beat the same month of the prior year, and a breakdown by airline.

Key insights
- SkyConnect Airways is by far the largest carrier: 1,307 completed flights in the current month and 1,283 in the previous month, far ahead of the other members, with revenue passenger kilometres of 1.78B this month and 1.85B the month before.
- On-time performance for the alliance is 84.4% in the selected month, among the year's highest with 84.5% in March, while April, February and August are the low months at 82.0%, 82.3% and 82.6%. Global Star is the most punctual airline at 94.4% and Pacific Wings the least at 77.3%; SkyConnect Airways' previous-month rate of 82.5% was also low.
- Alliance revenue passenger kilometres were lowest in February at 1.74B. The average CSAT score is 7.9 in the selected month, a high for the year, with February the low at 7.8; Pacific Wings has the lowest CSAT at 7.8 and Atlantic Express scored 7.9 in the previous month.
- New York is the top destination with 278 completed flights this month.
- Among aircraft, the B787 has the highest load factor at 91.1% while the A330 has the lowest at 89.6%; the B777 carried the most passengers in the previous month, 100,328, and the B787 flew the fewest flights that month, 275.
- Baggage mishandling is high at Atlantic Express (91.5% in the previous month) and Pacific Wings (86.7% this month).

Comp Flights BAN, Comp Flights Bars, Comp Flights Circles, Comp Flights Labels, Comp Flights Airlines
Completed flights for the month are 1,688, up 0.7% versus the previous month. SkyConnect Airways completed by far the most flights at 1,307, ahead of Atlantic Express (188), Pacific Wings (105) and Global Star (88).

On Time BAN, On Time Bars, On Time Circles, On Time Labels, On Time Airlines
On-time performance is 84.4%, up 2.3% versus the previous month. Global Star leads at 94.4%, followed by Atlantic Express (84.5%), SkyConnect Airways (84.3%) and Pacific Wings (77.3%).

RPK BAN, RPK Bars, RPK Circles, RPK Labels, RPK Airlines
Revenue passenger kilometres are 2.38 billion km, down 3.8% versus the previous month. SkyConnect Airways accounts for most of them at 1.78 billion km, followed by Global Star (0.32 billion), Atlantic Express (0.22 billion) and Pacific Wings (0.06 billion).

CSAT BAN, CSAT Bars, CSAT Circles, CSAT Labels, CSAT Airlines
The average satisfaction score is 7.9, down 0.2% versus the previous month. Global Star, Atlantic Express and SkyConnect Airways all score 7.9 and Pacific Wings 7.8.

Top Destinations
The top flight destinations in North America: New York with 278 flights, then Toronto (69), Vancouver (58), Boston (56) and Chicago (46).

Main Flight Times
A heat map of flights by month and day of the week; the darkest cells are the busiest, and the labelled low and high are 201 and 333 flights.

Aircraft Utilization
Completed flights and average load factor by aircraft type, each compared with the previous month: the B787 flew the most (317 flights) with the highest load factor (91.1%), followed by the B777 (315 flights, 90.7%), the A330 (293, 89.6%), the B737 (289, 90.3%), the A320 (281, 90.0%) and the A350 (280, 90.4%).

Mishandling, Baggage Airlines
The flights-with-baggage-mishandling indicator stands at 78.7% overall; by airline it is 86.7% for Pacific Wings, 83.5% for Atlantic Express, 79.5% for Global Star and 77.3% for SkyConnect Airways.

Years, Months, Selected Region, Airline Navigation, Logged in, Hide Guidelines, Show Guidelines
The dashboard's controls: the year and month buttons, the region drop-down, the navigation menu to the airline, flight and fleet pages, the login greeting and the guideline toggles. They carry no measures of their own.

expected.insightNarrative:
Dashboard 1 is the Boston Marathon Data Explorer: every finisher of the Boston Marathon from 1990 to 2025, 663,035 in total, with the field split between men and women, the distribution of finish times, the number of finishers per year and the ten fastest men and women with the weather on their race day. The controls at the top are set to the years 1990 to 2025, all age brackets, both genders, Split Men and Women on, Show Top X at 10 and Temperature Type at Temperature. The story is a race dominated in numbers by men under 40, a field that has more than doubled since 1990, and course records set in 2011 and 2025.

Key insights
- Men under 40 are the largest group of finishers by far: 200,317, or 30.22% of all 663,035 finishers.
- Finish times for men cluster around 3:30 and for women around 3:50 to 4:00, with long tails out to 7:00.
- Men's finishers rose from about 6,500 a year in 1990 to about 16,000 in 2025 and women's from about 2,000 to about 12,000; the 1996 centennial race spiked to nearly 30,000 men, and 2020 shows no finishers.
- The fastest men's times are Geoffrey Mutai's 2:03:02 and Moses Mosop's 2:03:06 in 2011; the fastest women's are Sharon Lokedi's 2:17:22 and Hellen Obiri's 2:17:41 in 2025.

Total
Total finishers: 663,035 for the selected years, age brackets and genders.

Gender Age Pie
The split of finishers by gender and age bracket as a donut: men under 40 are the largest slice at 200,317 finishers (30.22% of the total), followed by men 40 and over, women under 40 and women 40 and over.

Time Distribution
The distribution of finish times from 2:00 to 7:00 as a share of finishers, men in green and women in red: men peak at about 1.3% of finishers just after 3:00 and again near 3:30, women peak at about 1.3% between 3:45 and 4:00, and both curves taper to zero by about 6:30.

Finishers Over Time
Finishers per year from 1990 to 2025: men (green) grow from about 6,500 to about 16,000 and women (red) from about 2,000 to about 12,000, with a spike to nearly 30,000 men in the 1996 centennial race, a jump in 2014, a drop in 2020 when no finishers are recorded, and a dip in 2021 before the recovery.

Top Finishers
The ten fastest men and women with the weather at the start and finish: men led by Geoffrey Mutai (2011, 2:03:02), Moses Mosop (2011, 2:03:06), John Korir (2025, 2:04:45), Gebregziabher Gebremariam (2011, 2:04:53) and Ryan Hall (2011, 2:04:58), then Alphonce Felix Simbu and Cybrian Kotut (2025, 2:05:04), Conner Mantz (2025, 2:05:08), Robert Kiprono Cheruiyot (2010, 2:05:52) and Evans Chebet (2023, 2:05:54); women led by Sharon Lokedi (2025, 2:17:22), Hellen Obiri (2025, 2:17:41), Yalemzerf Yehualaw (2025, 2:18:06), Buzunesh Deba (2014, 2:19:59), Mare Dibaba (2014, 2:20:35), Jemima Jelagat Sumgong (2014, 2:20:41), Margaret Okayo (2002, 2:20:43), Peres Jepchirchir (2022, 2:21:01) and Ababel Yeshaneh (2022, 2:21:05). Dashboard 1 is the Boston Marathon Data Explorer: every finisher of the Boston Marathon from 1990 to 2025, 663,035 in total, with the field split between men and women, the distribution of finish times, the number of finishers per year and the ten fastest men and women with the weather on their race day. The controls at the top are set to the years 1990 to 2025, all age brackets, both genders, Split Men and Women on, Show Top X at 10 and Temperature Type at Temperature. The story is a race dominated in numbers by men under 40, a field that has more than doubled since 1990, and course records set in 2011 and 2025.

Key insights
- Men under 40 are the largest group of finishers by far: 200,317, or 30.22% of all 663,035 finishers.
- Finish times for men cluster around 3:30 and for women around 3:50 to 4:00, with long tails out to 7:00.
- Men's finishers rose from about 6,500 a year in 1990 to about 16,000 in 2025 and women's from about 2,000 to about 12,000; the 1996 centennial race spiked to nearly 30,000 men, and 2020 shows no finishers.
- The fastest men's times are Geoffrey Mutai's 2:03:02 and Moses Mosop's 2:03:06 in 2011; the fastest women's are Sharon Lokedi's 2:17:22 and Hellen Obiri's 2:17:41 in 2025.

Total
Total finishers: 663,035 for the selected years, age brackets and genders.

Gender Age Pie
The split of finishers by gender and age bracket as a donut: men under 40 are the largest slice at 200,317 finishers (30.22% of the total), followed by men 40 and over, women under 40 and women 40 and over.

Time Distribution
The distribution of finish times from 2:00 to 7:00 as a share of finishers, men in green and women in red: men peak at about 1.3% of finishers just after 3:00 and again near 3:30, women peak at about 1.3% between 3:45 and 4:00, and both curves taper to zero by about 6:30.

Finishers Over Time
Finishers per year from 1990 to 2025: men (green) grow from about 6,500 to about 16,000 and women (red) from about 2,000 to about 12,000, with a spike to nearly 30,000 men in the 1996 centennial race, a jump in 2014, a drop in 2020 when no finishers are recorded, and a dip in 2021 before the recovery.

Top Finishers
The ten fastest men and women with the weather at the start and finish: men led by Geoffrey Mutai (2011, 2:03:02), Moses Mosop (2011, 2:03:06), John Korir (2025, 2:04:45), Gebregziabher Gebremariam (2011, 2:04:53) and Ryan Hall (2011, 2:04:58), then Alphonce Felix Simbu and Cybrian Kotut (2025, 2:05:04), Conner Mantz (2025, 2:05:08), Robert Kiprono Cheruiyot (2010, 2:05:52) and Evans Chebet (2023, 2:05:54); women led by Sharon Lokedi (2025, 2:17:22), Hellen Obiri (2025, 2:17:41), Yalemzerf Yehualaw (2025, 2:18:06), Buzunesh Deba (2014, 2:19:59), Mare Dibaba (2014, 2:20:35), Jemima Jelagat Sumgong (2014, 2:20:41), Margaret Okayo (2002, 2:20:43), Peres Jepchirchir (2022, 2:21:01) and Ababel Yeshaneh (2022, 2:21:05). The 2011 records came on a 46F to 55F day with a 12 mph easterly tailwind; the 2025 times on a 51F to 54F day with a 3 to 8 mph wind from the northwest.

- Germany reported the most new positive cases, 87,298 (13.8% of the total), followed by the United States with 81,723 (12.9%) and Italy with 59,395 (9.4%).

- Thailand stands out on new deaths with 255.
- At the bottom of the ranking, Zambia, Yemen and the Winter Olympics 2022 entry reported 0 new cases.
- Globally, new positive cases are 631,675, down 13.0% from 725,664 the previous day, and new deaths are 2,507, down 16.0% from 2,985; daily cases peaked above 4M in January 2022, while daily deaths peaked near 20K in early and mid 2021 and have been falling since.

expected.insightNarrative:
Commission Model is the Sales Commission Model dashboard: enter a new quota, the quota for bonus attainment, the base salary and the commission rate to estimate the compensation of each sales rep under those conditions. The dashboard is set to a new quota of $450K, a bonus for $10,000, a base salary of $30,000 and a commission rate of 5.0%.

Key insights
- Richard Martinez is the outlier on every measure: $1,144,601 in sales, 254% of quota achieved, $1,145K of estimated achievement, $57,230 in commission pay and $97,230 in total compensation, the highest on the team.
- Behind him, Robert Wilson reaches 224% of quota, James Williams 154% ($79K of compensation), John Jones 146% ($68K), Charles Lee and Ruth Hernandez 122% ($67K), Michael Moore and Sharon King 117% ($65K) and Patricia Johnson and Margaret White 106% ($63K, the on-target earnings).
- Carol Allen sits exactly at 100% of quota, while Nancy Garcia, Lisa Martin (93%), David Thompson, Barbara Davis (90%), Thomas Young and Joseph Hall (83%) fall short and earn $49K to $51K.

Types of Pay
The resulting totals across the sales team: total base pay $1,230K, commission pay $780K and total bonus compensation $130K.

Cost of Seller Pay
Seller pay as a percent of total sales is 13.7%, and incentive pay as a percent of compensation is 42.5%.

Sales Planning
Performance and compensation by sales rep under these conditions. The left bars show each rep's sales against the new quota of $450K, coloured by quota attainment (below 50%, 50-75%, 75-100%, 100%+); the right bars show total compensation split into base salary, commission and bonus pay, with on-target earnings of $63K marked. Richard Martinez leads with 224% attainment and $97K of compensation, followed by Robert Wilson, James Williams (154%, $79K), Elizabeth Miller and Jessica Baker ($74K), John Jones (146%, $68K), Charles Lee and Ruth Hernandez (122%, $67K), Michael Moore and Sharon King (117%, $65K), Patricia Johnson and Margaret White (106%, $63K); Carol Allen is at 100% and Nancy Garcia, Lisa Martin (93%), David Thompson, Barbara Davis (90%), Thomas Young and Joseph Hall (83%) fall short of quota, earning $49K to $51K.

The title and the parameter controls at the top of the dashboard.

The title and the parameter controls at the top of the dashboard.

expected.insightNarrative:
Correlation Dashboard shows rating correlations by customer segment from a customer satisfaction survey. It is a single grid of nine scatter plots: three outcome ratings on the rows, Expertise Rating, Satisfaction Rating and Recommendation Rating, each from 0 to 10, against three drivers on the columns, How Easy to Buy, How Easy to Use and How Reliable, each scored 1 to 10. The filters Industry and Job Function are both set to All.

Key insights
- The largest response groups are all customers of 2+ years: male respondents in Accounting working in Finance (59 records), Sales (45), Other (38) and Marketing (36), and female respondents in Construction working in Finance (34).
- In every plot the trend lines slope upward: the easier a product is to buy and to use, and the more reliable it is, the higher the expertise, satisfaction and recommendation ratings.
- Customers of 2+ years sit highest and their trend lines start higher; customers of 1 year or less start lowest on satisfaction and recommendation.

Correlation
Each dot is a group of survey responses, sized by the number of records (from 1 to 59) and coloured by length of being a customer: 1 year or less, 1+ to 2 years, and 2+ years. A dashed trend line is drawn per customer-length group in each plot. The responses cluster in the upper right of every plot, with driver scores of roughly 6 to 10 matching outcome ratings of roughly 6 to 10, and all trend lines slope upward: the easier a product is to buy and use and the more reliable it is, the higher the expertise, satisfaction and recommendation ratings. Customers of 2+ years (blue) sit highest and their trend lines start higher, while the newest customers (olive) start lowest on the satisfaction and recommendation rows.

expected.insightNarrative:
Employee Churn is the churn page of the HR Workforce accelerator for Salesforce: which organizations and departments were the most impacted by employee churn over the last twelve months, from Dec-21 to Dec-22, and which require special attention because of a high churn risk. The filters at the top are set to the current month Dec, the current year 2022, and All for department, nationality, gender and organization.

Key insights
- The employee churn rate is 27.2% on an average headcount of 389.2, with (106) leavers and +59 starters over the last 12 months.
- DE Subsidiary's Production department is the most affected team: 26 leavers in the last 12 months on the largest average headcount, 94.2. US Subsidiary's Sales department is the other large team, with an average headcount of 46.5.
- Hiring was strongest in DE Subsidiary's Client Services and Holding's General Management, each with +5 starters in the last 12 months.
- Over the period, starters peaked in May 2021 with +42 (a net +35 after leavers), leavers peaked in September 2022 with -23, and FTE fell to its lowest at 344 in November 2022 and 336 in December 2022.

Employee Churn KPIs, Perf - Analyzed Period for 12 months
The employee churn rate is 27.2% on an average headcount of 389.2, with (106) leavers and +59 starters, computed on the last 12 months, from Dec-21 to Dec-22.

Dept/Org - Churn Risk
ACTUAL CHURN: which organizations and departments were the most impacted by employee churn. A grid of organizations (DE Subsidiary, US Subsidiary, Holding, PT Subsidiary, SP Subsidiary, Optys Corp., CH Subsidiary) by department (Production, Sales, General Management, ICT, Client Services, Marketing, Procurement, Finance, Quality Department, Board of Advisors, Real Estate, Human Resources, Research & Development) shows one square per team, sized by leavers and coloured by churn rate. The largest loss is DE Subsidiary Production with 26 leavers on an average headcount of 94.2; US Subsidiary Finance lost 9, Holding Marketing 9, Holding General Management 8, Holding Research & Development 7, Holding ICT 6 and SP Subsidiary Real Estate 6; most other teams lost between one and five people. DE Subsidiary Client Services and Holding General Management each gained 5 starters, and US Subsidiary Sales has an average headcount of 46.5.

Employee per Dept/Org - Churn Risk
UPCOMING CHURN RISK: which organizations and departments require special attention because of a high churn risk. The same organizations by department, one circle per employee coloured by churn risk, where concentrations of red dots mark teams with a high churn risk. The largest teams are DE Subsidiary Production, US Subsidiary Supply Chain and Sales, and PT Subsidiary Production; the orange dots that flag risk are concentrated in DE Subsidiary Production and Quality Department, Holding General Management, Marketing and Finance, and SP Subsidiary General Management and Real Estate.

Starters and Leavers Evolution
The month-by-month evolution of starters, leavers and FTE behind the page: starters peaked in May 2021 with +42 (a net +35 after leavers), leavers peaked in September 2022 with -23, and FTE fell to 344 in November 2022 and 336 in December 2022, the lowest of the period.

expected.insightNarrative:
Employee Churn is the churn page of the HR Workforce accelerator for Salesforce: which organizations and departments were the most impacted by employee churn over the last twelve months, from Dec-21 to Dec-22, and which require special attention because of a high churn risk. The filters at the top are set to the current month Dec, the current year 2022, and All for department, nationality, gender and organization.

Key insights
- The employee churn rate is 27.2% on an average headcount of 389.2, with (106) leavers and +59 starters over the last 12 months.
- DE Subsidiary's Production department is the most affected team: 26 leavers in the last 12 months on the largest average headcount, 94.2. US Subsidiary's Sales department is the other large team, with an average headcount of 46.5.
- Hiring was strongest in DE Subsidiary's Client Services and Holding's General Management, each with +5 starters in the last 12 months.
- Over the period, starters peaked in May 2021 with +42 (a net +35 after leavers), leavers peaked in September 2022 with -23, and FTE fell to its lowest at 344 in November 2022 and 336 in December 2022.

Employee Churn KPIs, Perf - Analyzed Period for 12 months
The employee churn rate is 27.2% on an average headcount of 389.2, with (106) leavers and +59 starters, computed on the last 12 months, from Dec-21 to Dec-22.

Dept/Org - Churn Risk
ACTUAL CHURN: which organizations and departments were the most impacted by employee churn. A grid of organizations (DE Subsidiary, US Subsidiary, Holding, PT Subsidiary, SP Subsidiary, Optys Corp., CH Subsidiary) by department (Production, Sales, General Management, ICT, Client Services, Marketing, Procurement, Finance, Quality Department, Board of Advisors, Real Estate, Human Resources, Research & Development) shows one square per team, sized by leavers and coloured by churn rate. The largest loss is DE Subsidiary Production with 26 leavers on an average headcount of 94.2; US Subsidiary Finance lost 9, Holding Marketing 9, Holding General Management 8, Holding Research & Development 7, Holding ICT 6 and SP Subsidiary Real Estate 6; most other teams lost between one and five people. DE Subsidiary Client Services and Holding General Management each gained 5 starters, and US Subsidiary Sales has an average headcount of 46.5.

Employee per Dept/Org - Churn Risk
UPCOMING CHURN RISK: which organizations and departments require special attention because of a high churn risk. The same organizations by department, one circle per employee coloured by churn risk, where concentrations of red dots mark teams with a high churn risk. The largest teams are DE Subsidiary Production, US Subsidiary Supply Chain and Sales, and PT Subsidiary Production; the orange dots that flag risk are concentrated in DE Subsidiary Production and Quality Department, Holding General Management, Marketing and Finance, and SP Subsidiary General Management and Real Estate.

Starters and Leavers Evolution
The month-by-month evolution of starters, leavers and FTE behind the page: starters peaked in May 2021 with +42 (a net +35 after leavers), leavers peaked in September 2022 with -23, and FTE fell to 344 in November 2022 and 336 in December 2022, the lowest of the period.

expected.insightNarrative:
Expenses Audit is an expense audit dashboard for 2021 compared with 2020: KPI tiles for total expenses, the average claim and the number of claims, each with a monthly line against the prior year, the total by department against the prior year, the top 15 employees by expenses, an expense-type drilldown and a table of duplicate payments. Total expenses for 2021 are £517.1K, down 2.8% on 2020, from 4,955 claims (down 1.8%) averaging £104.35 (up 1.0%). The story is a spend concentrated in three departments and a handful of senior job titles, with May 2020 the busiest month of the two years and June 2021 the quietest, and four employees with duplicate claims.

Key insights
- By department, Training spent the most in 2021 at £66.7K (12.9% of the total), followed by Business Development at £64.3K (12.4%) and Accounting at £61.4K (11.9%); Human Resources and Sales spent the least at £22.2K each (4.3%), with Support at £29.7K (5.7%).
- By job title, Associates account for £89.7K (17.3%), Senior Analysts £86.7K (16.8%) and Senior Associates £76.4K (14.8%), while VPs account for the least at £52.8K (10.2%), Managers £66.4K (12.8%) and Analysts £71.4K (13.8%).
- The top individual spenders are Ruddie Itzhayek with £6.9K, Adela Swepson with £6.7K and Janeczka Ecles with £6.7K (1.3% each); the lowest are Kippar Verbrugge (£2.9K), Eve Nizet (£3.5K) and Marice Baudouin (£3.8K).
- Monthly totals peaked in May 2020 at £50.4K, with 455 claims that month, and were lowest in June 2021 at £36.2K with 356 claims; February 2021 (370 claims) and April 2020 (386) were also low months, and January 2021 was high with 445 claims.
- The average claim was highest in August 2021 (£111.35), September 2020 (£110.97) and May 2020 (£110.71).
- Among expense types, Other is the largest at £106.3K and Consumables - Food & Drink the smallest at £99.1K in 2021.
- Duplicate payments concentrate on three people, Trevar Nollet (£276.9, 31.0%), Granger Tipler (£254.6, 28.5%) and Alford Gentzsch (£143.0, 16.0%); on Senior Associates (59.5%), Analysts (30.4%) and Associates (10.1%); on Business Development (38.6%), Support (31.0%) and Accounting (16.0%); and on two expense types, Home Office Equipment (£487.6, 54.6%) and Mileage (£405.9, 45.4%).

Total Amount Lines
Total expenses of £517.1K for 2021, down 2.8% versus the prior year, with the monthly totals: a high of £50.4K in May 2020 and a low of £36.2K in June 2021.

Average Expense Claim Lines
The average claim is £104.35 for 2021, up 1.0% on the prior year; by month it was highest in August 2021 (£111.35), September 2020 (£110.97) and May 2020 (£110.71).

Total Number of Claims
4,955 claims in 2021, down 1.8% on the prior year; monthly highs of 455 in May 2020 and 445 in January 2021, lows of 356 in June 2021, 370 in February 2021 and 386 in April 2020.

Total Expense by Department (2)
2021 expenses by department against 2020: Training £66.7K, Business Development £64.3K and Accounting £61.4K at the top, then Product Management £53.0K, Marketing £44.5K, Engineering £41.0K, Legal £39.2K, Services £38.5K, Research and Development £34.5K and Support £29.7K, with Sales and Human Resources at £22.2K at the bottom; Accounting, Product Management, Marketing, Support and Sales spent more than in 2020.

Top 15 employees with expenses
Ruddie Itzhayek (£6,861.83 from 62 claims, up £2,243.4 or 48.6% on 2020), Adela Swepson (£6,743.44, 57 claims, down 18.9%) and Janeczka Ecles (£6,668.17, 55 claims, up 15.6%) lead, followed by Dolley Brambill (£6,630.15), Lexy Dagnall (£6,604.97), Davy Knath (£6,390.47, down 31.8%), Herbie Mokes (£6,342.30), Mariele Stivers (£6,292.62, up 47.2%), Rockey Antoniutti (£6,267.71, up 36.5%) and Corine Treneman (£6,256.77); by job title Associates, Senior Analysts and Senior Associates spend the most and VPs the least.

Expense Type Drilldown

expected.insightNarrative:
HLS Patient record is a patient record dashboard for a hospital group, built on the data of Tableau's Patient Record accelerator, covering August 2022 to July 2024. Six KPIs sit at the top, and clicking one shows it in the other views; the dashboard is set to Readmissions %, shown over time, by facility, by speciality and by doctor. The story is a readmission rate of 7.3% that spiked in the autumn of 2023 and is concentrated in one facility, two specialities and a few doctors.

Key insights
- Readmissions peaked in November 2023 at 12.3% and October 2023 at 11.2%, well above the average of about 7%, after a low of 3.8% in May 2023.
- Hospital 3 is the outlier among facilities with a 100% readmission rate; Hospital 4 follows at 28.6% and Hospital 5 at 11.2%, with Hospitals 2 and 1 under 10%.
- By speciality, Neonatalogy Sick Born (11.9%) and Ophtalmology (11.0%) have the highest readmission rates and Neonatalogy Healthy Born the lowest (1.5%), with Gastroenterology (4.3%) and Obstetric (4.8%) also low; Medecine is third highest at 9.0%.
- Doctor 00019 and Doctor 00054 have 100% readmission rates and Doctor 00052 50%, while Doctors 00039 and 00003 (11.1%) and 01678 (11.2%) are the lowest of the top 15.
- The other KPIs: average length of stay 3.89 days, 21,461 stays, 933 DRG high outliers, 8,491 emergency admissions and a cost-weight per stay of 0.5733.

KPIs
Avg. LOS (days) 3.89; Nb of Stays 21,461; Readmissions % 7.3%; DRG - Nb of High Outliers 933; Emergency Admissions 8,491; Cost-Weight per Stay 0.5733.

Trend Line
Readmissions % by month from May 2023 to July 2024 against an average of about 7%: from a low of 3.8% in May 2023 it climbs to the highs of 11.2% in October and 12.3% in November 2023, falls back to about 4.8% in January 2024, and then moves between about 5% and 7.5% through July 2024, ending near 5.7%.

Facility lolipop
Readmissions % by facility, click to filter: Hospital 3 at 100%, Hospital 4 at 28.6%, Hospital 5 at 11.2%, and Hospitals 2 and 1 under 10%.

Speciality lolipop
Readmissions % by speciality: Neonatalogy Sick Born highest at 11.9%, then Ophtalmology at 11.0% and Medecine at 9.0%; Urology and Pediatrics about 8 to 9%, General surgery, Gynecology, ENT, Orthopedics and Obstetric (4.8%) about 5 to 7%, Gastroenterology 4.3%, and Neonatalogy Healthy Born lowest at 1.5%.

expected.insightNarrative:
Executive Summary is the executive page of the HR Headcount accelerator for Salesforce: the company's headcount, full-time equivalents and occupation rate as of December 2021, each against the previous month and the same month of the previous year, overall and by organization. The filters at the top are set to the current month Dec, the current year 2021, and All for organization and the other filters. The story is a workforce at its smallest in two years, shrinking fastest at Holding, while the occupation rate is at its highest.

Key insights
- Total headcount is at its lowest point of the two-year history: 364 in December 2021 after 375 in November and 387 in October, down 11 versus the previous month and down 57 versus December 2020.
- Total FTE is likewise at its lowest, 343.7 in December 2021 after 354.2 in November, down 10.5 on the month and 50.9 on the year.
- The occupation rate is at its highest, 94% in both November and December 2021 (94.4%), a level last seen in April 2020.
- DE Subsidiary is the largest organization with 139 employees and 125.9 FTE, but it lost 5 employees and 4.6 FTE in the month; Holding shows the steepest yearly decline, down 21 employees and 21.4 FTE versus December 2020.
- Optys Corp. has the lowest occupation rate, 87%, below target like DE Subsidiary's 91%.

Headcount KPI - Perf Card, $Headcount (advanced) - KPIs Headcount variances, Headcount (advanced) - Cockpit Label - Previous Month, Headcount (advanced) - Cockpit Label - Same Month Previous Year
Total headcount is 364 as of Dec-2021, down 11 (-2.9%) versus November 2021 and down 57 (-13.5%) versus December 2020, with a sparkline of the last twelve months.

Occupation Rate KPI - Perf Card (bar chart), Total FTE KPI - Perf Card (line chart), $Headcount (advanced) - KPIs FTE variances
The occupation rate is 94% and the total FTE 343.7 as of Dec-2021, the FTE down 10.5 (-3.0%) versus the previous month and down 50.9 (-12.9%) versus the previous year.

$Top Organizations - Headcount - Perf Bar, $Top Organizations - Headcount - Mini Trend
Total headcount by organization as of Dec-2021, with its twelve-month trend and its change versus November 2021 and December 2020: DE Subsidiary 139 (down 5 versus the previous month, down 15 versus the previous year), US Subsidiary 110 (down 2, down 11), Holding 72 (down 4, down 21), PT Subsidiary 29 (down 4 versus the previous year), SP Subsidiary 10 (down 4 versus the previous year), Optys Corp. 3 (down 1) and CH Subsidiary 1 (down 1).

$Top Organizations - Occupation Rate - Perf Bar
The occupation rate by organization: 91% for DE Subsidiary and 87% for Optys Corp., both marked in orange as below target, and 98% for US Subsidiary, 95% for Holding, 98% for PT Subsidiary, 99% for SP Subsidiary and 100% for CH Subsidiary.

$Top Organizations - FTE - Perf Bar, $Top Organizations - FTE - Mini Trend
Total FTE by organization as of Dec-2021 with its changes: DE Subsidiary 125.9 (down 4.6 versus the previous month, down 10.3 versus the previous year), US Subsidiary 107.7 (down 2.0, down 9.9), Holding 68.3 (down 3.9, down 21.4), PT Subsidiary 28.3 (down 3.7 versus the previous year), SP Subsidiary 9.9 (down 3.6), Optys Corp. 2.6 (down 1.0) and CH Subsidiary 1.0 (down 1.0).

expected.insightNarrative:
NHS Hospital Admitted Patient Care shows the admitted patient care activity of the NHS for 2019 to 2020: six KPI tiles at the top, the finished consultant episodes by gender and main speciality, episodes against mean age by gender, a Pareto chart of admissions by speciality, the mean length of stay and mean time waited by speciality, and the mix of admission types per speciality. The story is activity concentrated in a few large specialities, General Medicine and General Surgery above all, with psychiatry holding patients longest and geriatric medicine making them wait longest.

Key insights
- General Medicine and General Surgery are the largest specialities for both genders: 1.8M (15.8%) and 1.1M (9.5%) female episodes, 1.6M (17.3%) and 964.8K (10.2%) male episodes, followed by Gynaecology (768.8K, 6.7%) for women and Paediatrics (798.4K, 8.4%) for men.
- Admissions follow the same pattern: General Medicine 2,374,451 (13.8%), General Surgery 1,848,911 (10.7%), Paediatrics 1,403,182 (8.2%), Gastroenterology 1,224,422 and Trauma & Orthopaedics 1,065,766 lead, and about 80% of admissions fall in 14 specialities; Medical Virology (0), Sports & Exercise Medicine (2) and Occupational Medicine (4) have almost none.
- Episodes of unknown gender are concentrated in two specialities: Ophthalmology (3,791, 37.9%) and Geriatric Medicine (3,162, 31.6%) make up 69.4% of them, with 83 other specialities sharing the remaining 3.1K.
- Forensic Psychiatry has by far the longest mean length of stay, 372.9 days (30.3% of the total across specialities), ahead of Old Age Psychiatry at 82.1 and non-UK providers at 73.2; General Dental Practice (0) and Community Health Services Dental (0.17) are the shortest.
- Geriatric Medicine has the longest mean time waited, 244.3 days, followed by Orthodontics (161.8), Anaesthetics (136.7), Critical Care Medicine (129.9) and Clinical Physiology (112.4); Psychotherapy (5), Child & Adolescent Psychiatry (6.0) and Old Age Psychiatry (7) are the shortest.
- Admission types differ sharply by speciality: Midwife episodes (96.7%), Obstetrics (87.3%), Community Medicine (68.6%) and General Medical Practice (58.9%) are mostly "other" admissions, Immunopathology (91.7%), Periodontics (88%) and Clinical Physiology (85%) are mostly planned, and Accident & Emergency (99%), Endodontics (97%) and Acute Internal Medicine (97%) are almost all emergencies.
- The mean age is highest in General Medical Practice (80.8), Geriatric Medicine (79.1) and Community Medicine (76.8) and lowest in Paediatrics (3.0), Paediatric Surgery (6.7) and Paediatric Cardiology (7.7).

Episodes by Gender- Female, Episodes by Gender- Male, Episodes by Gender- Unknown
Finished consultant episodes by main speciality for each gender: General Medicine and General Surgery rank first and second for both women (1.8M and 1.1M) and men (1.6M and 964.8K), with Gynaecology third for women and Paediatrics third for men; among episodes of unknown gender Ophthalmology (3.8K) and Geriatric Medicine (3.2K) dominate, and Tropical Medicine, Surgical Dentistry and Sports & Exercise Medicine have none.

Episodes vs. Mean Age by Gender
Episodes plotted against mean age for each gender and speciality: the largest points are General Medicine (1,806,137 female and 1,644,290 male episodes) and General Surgery (964,821 male), and the unknown-gender points for Ophthalmology (3,791) and Geriatric Medicine (3,162) stand out; the oldest patients are in General Medical Practice, Geriatric Medicine and Community Medicine, the youngest in the paediatric specialities.

Pareto Chart
Admissions by speciality with the cumulative share: General Medicine (2,374,451), General Surgery (1,848,911), Paediatrics (1,403,182), Gastroenterology (1,224,422) and Trauma & Orthopaedics (1,065,766) lead, and 80% of admissions are concentrated in 14 specialities.

Mean LOS
The mean length of stay by speciality: Forensic Psychiatry is the outlier at 372.9 days, then Old Age Psychiatry at 82.1 and non-UK providers at 73.2; dental specialities are the shortest.

Mean Time Waited
The mean time waited by speciality: Geriatric Medicine (244.3), Orthodontics (161.8), Anaesthetics (136.7), Critical Care Medicine (129.9) and Clinical Physiology (112.4) wait longest; Psychotherapy, Child & Adolescent Psychiatry and Old Age Psychiatry wait least.

Types of Admissions (%)
The share of emergency, waiting list, planned and other admissions per speciality: Midwife episodes, Obstetrics, Community Medicine and General Medical Practice are mostly other admissions; Immunopathology, Periodontics and Clinical Physiology mostly planned; Accident & Emergency, Endodontics and Acute Internal Medicine almost entirely emergency; the dental specialities are almost entirely waiting list.

expected.insightNarrative:
NHS Hospital Admitted Patient Care shows the admitted patient care activity of the NHS for 2019 to 2020: six KPI tiles at the top, the finished consultant episodes by gender and main speciality, episodes against mean age by gender, a Pareto chart of admissions by speciality, the mean length of stay and mean time waited by speciality, and the mix of admission types per speciality. The story is activity concentrated in a few large specialities, General Medicine and General Surgery above all, with psychiatry holding patients longest and geriatric medicine making them wait longest.

Key insights
- General Medicine and General Surgery are the largest specialities for both genders: 1.8M (15.8%) and 1.1M (9.5%) female episodes, 1.6M (17.3%) and 964.8K (10.2%) male episodes, followed by Gynaecology (768.8K, 6.7%) for women and Paediatrics (798.4K, 8.4%) for men.
- Admissions follow the same pattern: General Medicine 2,374,451 (13.8%), General Surgery 1,848,911 (10.7%), Paediatrics 1,403,182 (8.2%), Gastroenterology 1,224,422 and Trauma & Orthopaedics 1,065,766 lead, and about 80% of admissions fall in 14 specialities; Medical Virology (0), Sports & Exercise Medicine (2) and Occupational Medicine (4) have almost none.
- Episodes of unknown gender are concentrated in two specialities: Ophthalmology (3,791, 37.9%) and Geriatric Medicine (3,162, 31.6%) make up 69.4% of them, with 83 other specialities sharing the remaining 3.1K.
- Forensic Psychiatry has by far the longest mean length of stay, 372.9 days (30.3% of the total across specialities), ahead of Old Age Psychiatry at 82.1 and non-UK providers at 73.2; General Dental Practice (0) and Community Health Services Dental (0.17) are the shortest.
- Geriatric Medicine has the longest mean time waited, 244.3 days, followed by Orthodontics (161.8), Anaesthetics (136.7), Critical Care Medicine (129.9) and Clinical Physiology (112.4); Psychotherapy (5), Child & Adolescent Psychiatry (6.0) and Old Age Psychiatry (7) are the shortest.
- Admission types differ sharply by speciality: Midwife episodes (96.7%), Obstetrics (87.3%), Community Medicine (68.6%) and General Medical Practice (58.9%) are mostly "other" admissions, Immunopathology (91.7%), Periodontics (88%) and Clinical Physiology (85%) are mostly planned, and Accident & Emergency (99%), Endodontics (97%) and Acute Internal Medicine (97%) are almost all emergencies.
- The mean age is highest in General Medical Practice (80.8), Geriatric Medicine (79.1) and Community Medicine (76.8) and lowest in Paediatrics (3.0), Paediatric Surgery (6.7) and Paediatric Cardiology (7.7).

Episodes by Gender- Female, Episodes by Gender- Male, Episodes by Gender- Unknown
Finished consultant episodes by main speciality for each gender: General Medicine and General Surgery rank first and second for both women (1.8M and 1.1M) and men (1.6M and 964.8K), with Gynaecology third for women and Paediatrics third for men; among episodes of unknown gender Ophthalmology (3.8K) and Geriatric Medicine (3.2K) dominate, and Tropical Medicine, Surgical Dentistry and Sports & Exercise Medicine have none.

Episodes vs. Mean Age by Gender
Episodes plotted against mean age for each gender and speciality: the largest points are General Medicine (1,806,137 female and 1,644,290 male episodes) and General Surgery (964,821 male), and the unknown-gender points for Ophthalmology (3,791) and Geriatric Medicine (3,162) stand out; the oldest patients are in General Medical Practice, Geriatric Medicine and Community Medicine, the youngest in the paediatric specialities.

Pareto Chart
Admissions by speciality with the cumulative share: General Medicine (2,374,451), General Surgery (1,848,911), Paediatrics (1,403,182), Gastroenterology (1,224,422) and Trauma & Orthopaedics (1,065,766) lead, and 80% of admissions are concentrated in 14 specialities.

Mean LOS
The mean length of stay by speciality: Forensic Psychiatry is the outlier at 372.9 days, then Old Age Psychiatry at 82.1 and non-UK providers at 73.2; dental specialities are the shortest.

Mean Time Waited
The mean time waited by speciality: Geriatric Medicine (244.3), Orthodontics (161.8), Anaesthetics (136.7), Critical Care Medicine (129.9) and Clinical Physiology (112.4) wait longest; Psychotherapy, Child & Adolescent Psychiatry and Old Age Psychiatry wait least.

Types of Admissions (%)
The share of emergency, waiting list, planned and other admissions per speciality: Midwife episodes, Obstetrics, Community Medicine and General Medical Practice are mostly other admissions; Immunopathology, Periodontics and Clinical Physiology mostly planned; Accident & Emergency, Endodontics and Acute Internal Medicine almost entirely emergency; the dental specialities are almost entirely waiting list.

expected.insightNarrative:
Profitability KPI tracks the profitability of a shipping business per shipment and per company: by knowing which companies bring the most or least profit, better decisions can be made about which to keep. The story is three customers bringing three quarters of the profit, one of them, Eliza Software, at an unusually high margin, and a few shipments whose discounts wipe out their profit.

Key insights
- Eliza Software stands out with an average profit ratio per shipment of 36.9%, far above every other company; the lowest ratios belong to Endova Corp (7.9%), Aqua LLC (8.3%) and Blue Heron (8.9%).
- Anova (25.7% of profit), Eliza Software (25.5%) and Spirit Soda (23.3%) bring about three quarters of the total profit.
- The deepest discounts in the shipment detail are on two Firebright shipments (-$593 on shipment 991918 with a pay amount of $1,178 and -$328 on 991324), a Koncept shipment (-$539 on 997312, pay amount $1,960) and two Anova shipments (-$275 on 991435 and -$256 on 992032).

Profitability
Profitability per shipment as a scatter plot of profit ratio per shipment against profit, with each shipment rated GOOD (blue), OK (orange) or BAD (red). Most shipments sit between $0 and $2,000 of profit with ratios below 100%; a handful reach $2,000 to $6,000 of profit, two shipments exceed a 400% ratio, and the BAD shipments cluster at or below $0 profit with negative ratios.

Profitability by Company
The share of total profit and the profit ratio by company, sorted by share, with a search box for a shipment ID and click-to-filter. Anova (25.7%, ratio 20.4%), Eliza Software (25.5%, 36.9%) and Spirit Soda (23.3%, 16.1%) bring three quarters of the profit; Firebright (5.5%), Accent on Style (3.8%) and Kyle Industries (3.7%) follow; the remaining companies, from Viktoria's (2.8%) down to Blue Heron (0.0%), each contribute under 3%, with the lowest ratios at Endova Corp (7.9%), Aqua LLC (8.3%) and Blue Heron (8.9%).

Profitability Details
A table of shipments for the selected customer (Accent on Style): shipment ID, pay amount and a set of rating flags per shipment, with pay amounts from $324.94 to $1,050.

expected.insightNarrative:
US_View is the Revenue by State dashboard for the United States: total revenue for the selected period on a hexagon map of the states, the same revenue ranked by state, and the invoice lines behind it at chart-of-account level. The selectors at the top are set to the period January 2021, state All and city All; clicking a state on the map filters the bar chart and the detailed view, and clicking a bar filters the detailed view. The story is revenue concentrated in California, which brings more than twice the revenue of any other state.

Key insights
- California leads with $1,125K of revenue, more than double the next state.
- New Jersey ($510K), Florida ($508K), Texas ($469K) and Illinois ($449K) form the next tier, followed by Pennsylvania ($430K), New York ($429K) and Massachusetts ($409K).
- The invoice lines behind the map total $8,898,330, with the largest single lines in New York, Salt Lake City, Chicago, San Francisco and Los Angeles.

HexBin Map
Total revenue by state as a hexagon map of the United States, one tile per state including Alaska, Hawaii, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico, shaded by revenue: California, Texas and Florida stand out as the darkest tiles.

Bar Chart
Total revenue by state, ranked: California leads with $1,125K, far ahead of New Jersey ($510K), Florida ($508K), Texas ($469K), Illinois ($449K), Pennsylvania ($430K), New York ($429K) and Massachusetts ($409K); Ohio ($315K), Michigan ($296K) and Virginia ($283K) follow, with the remaining states lower down the list.

US Detailed View
The detailed view at chart-of-account level: one row per invoice line with company code (888), account (20624, 20697, 20681, 20638, 20636, 20643 and others), business unit (5557, 5565, 5569, 5616, 5717), profit center (778), state and city, and the amount. The grand total is $8,898,330. The largest lines shown are in New York ($479 and $448), Salt Lake City, Utah ($436 and $421), Chicago, Illinois ($416), New York ($410), San Francisco, California ($408 and $388), Los Angeles ($400), Newport Beach ($389) and New York ($388).

expected.insightNarrative:
Supply Chain is the RWFD Supply Chain Dashboard: four KPI tiles (orders per customer, total orders, average order weight and average units per order), carrier utilization, service level attainment, and five rankings of the plants by orders, unit quantity, order weight, ship-ahead days and ship-late days. Clicking a carrier name in Carrier Utilization filters the dashboard to that carrier. The story is a supply chain that runs through one plant: PLANT03 takes the bulk of the orders, units and weight, and also most of the early and late shipments.

expected.insightNarrative:
Website Traffic Overview is a web analytics dashboard for a site's traffic from May 2017 to August 2019: six KPI cards (total sessions, average session duration, bounce %, page views, average time on page and page exits %), each with its change year to date and a monthly trend, a scatter of bounce % against page exits % by referral source, and a panel of the six channel groupings with their sessions, session duration, unique pageviews and time on page. The story is a site whose traffic has grown many times over since its first months, driven by organic search, while the early months of 2017 explain most of the weak numbers.

Key insights
- Total sessions reached 30.1K, up 69.8% year to date, and page views 50.7K, up 117.6%; the average session lasts 67 seconds (up 36.2%), time on page is 30 seconds (up 3.2%), the bounce rate fell to 21% (down 11.8%) and page exits to 15% (down 24.3%).
- The site's first months were its weakest: 372 sessions in May 2017, 1,056 in June, 1,275 in July, 1,389 in August and 1,347 in September; October 2017 had the shortest sessions (19 seconds), the lowest unique pageviews (0.8 per session), the shortest time on page (20 seconds) and the highest page exits (37%). May 2017, by contrast, had the longest sessions (116 seconds), the longest time on page (35 seconds) and the lowest exits (10%).
- The bounce rate has fallen to its lowest levels in 2019: 19% in February, March, May and July and 20% in June.
- Organic Search is the main channel with 66,960 sessions (67.0K, up 49,623 on the reference period), ahead of Direct (37.9K) and Referral (11.9K); Social fell by 15,669 sessions, and Display (21 sessions) is negligible. Organic Search sessions peaked at 12,732 in August 2019, 10,695 in July and 8,691 in June; Direct peaked at 7,902 in April 2019.
- Referral visitors are the most engaged: 111.5 seconds per session, 2.1 unique pageviews and 36.9 seconds on page, with monthly highs of 2.5 pageviews in October 2018 and 45 seconds on page in February 2019; Display is the least engaged at 9.8 seconds per session (208 seconds below its reference of 218), 1.0 unique pageview and 7.9 seconds on page.
- Among referral sources, google.com.br (91,833 sessions), indiegogo.com (48,792), cnet.com (11,346) and amazon.co.jp (10,872) bring the most sessions; ask.com, biblegateway.com and canalblog.com have the highest bounce (0.50) and exit rates (ask.com 50% this month), while timesonline.co.uk, cnbc.com and 4shared.com bounce least.

Sessions, Bar - Sessions
Total sessions 30.1K, up 69.8% year to date; the monthly trend climbs steadily from the lows of 372 in May 2017 and 1,056 in June 2017.

Sessions Durations, Bar - Sessions duration
Average session duration 67 seconds, up 36.2%; May 2017 was the high at 116 seconds and October 2017 the low at 19 seconds, with July (37 s) and December 2017 (38 s) also low.

bounce %, Bar - bounce %
Bounce rate 21%, down 11.8%; the lowest months are February, March, May and July 2019 at 19% and June 2019 at 20%.

Total Unique pageview, Bar - unique pageviews
Page views 50.7K, up 117.6%; unique pageviews per session were lowest in October 2017 (0.8), July 2017 (1.0), December 2017 (1.1) and August and November 2017 (1.2).

Avg Time on Page, Bar - avg time on page
Average time on page 30 seconds, up 3.2%; the low was October 2017 (20 s) and the high May 2017 (35 s).

Avg Page exits, Bar - page load time
Page exits 15%, down 24.3%; October 2017 (37%), July 2017 (24%) and December 2017 (23%) were the high months and May 2017 (10%) the low.

Sheet 70
Bounce % against page exits % by referral source: most sources sit at 10 to 20% exits and 15 to 25% bounce, and the two move together; google.com.br (91,833 sessions), indiegogo.com (48,792), cnet.com (11,346) and amazon.co.jp (10,872) are the largest sources, and ask.com, biblegateway.com and canalblog.com the highest bouncing.

Top Dim - Total Sessions - Perf Card, Top Dim - Total Sessions - Mini Trend
Sessions by channel: Organic Search 67.0K (66,960, up 49,623), Direct 37.9K, Referral 11.9K, Paid Search 10.3K, Social 10.2K (down 15,669) and Display 21; Organic Search, Direct, Referral and Paid Search are rising while Social and Display fall, with Organic Search at 12,732 in August 2019.

Top Dim - Session Duration - Perf Card, Top Dim - Mini Trends (Session Duration) (line chart)
Session duration by channel: Referral 111.5 seconds, Organic Search 84.3, Social 52.2, Paid Search 48.7, Direct 47.2 and Display 9.8, which is 208 seconds below its 218-second reference.

Top Dim - Avg Unique Pageviews - Perf Card, Top Dim - Mini Trends (Avg Unique Pageviews) (bar chart)
Unique pageviews per session by channel: Referral 2.1, Organic Search 1.9, Paid Search 1.5, Social and Direct 1.3 and Display 1.0 (1.1 below its reference of 2.1); Referral peaked at 2.5 in October 2018 and 2.4 in February and March 2019, Display sat at 0.7 in February and March 2019.

Top Dim - Avg Time on Page - Perf Card, Top Dim - Mini Trends (Avg Time on Page) (line chart)
Time on page by channel: Referral 36.9 seconds, Organic Search 31.4, Social 29.8, Direct 27.4, Paid Search 23.4 and Display 7.9 (44 seconds below its 52-second reference); Referral peaked at 45 seconds in February 2019 and 43 in March 2019, Paid Search at 44 seconds in November 2018.

expected.insightNarrative:
Website Traffic Overview is a web analytics dashboard for a site's traffic from May 2017 to August 2019: six KPI cards (total sessions, average session duration, bounce %, page views, average time on page and page exits %), each with its change year to date and a monthly trend, a scatter of bounce % against page exits % by referral source, and a panel of the six channel groupings with their sessions, session duration, unique pageviews and time on page. The story is a site whose traffic has grown many times over since its first months, driven by organic search, while the early months of 2017 explain most of the weak numbers.

Key insights
- Total sessions reached 30.1K, up 69.8% year to date, and page views 50.7K, up 117.6%; the average session lasts 67 seconds (up 36.2%), time on page is 30 seconds (up 3.2%), the bounce rate fell to 21% (down 11.8%) and page exits to 15% (down 24.3%).
- The site's first months were its weakest: 372 sessions in May 2017, 1,056 in June, 1,275 in July, 1,389 in August and 1,347 in September; October 2017 had the shortest sessions (19 seconds), the lowest unique pageviews (0.8 per session), the shortest time on page (20 seconds) and the highest page exits (37%). May 2017, by contrast, had the longest sessions (116 seconds), the longest time on page (35 seconds) and the lowest exits (10%).
- The bounce rate has fallen to its lowest levels in 2019: 19% in February, March, May and July and 20% in June.
- Organic Search is the main channel with 66,960 sessions (67.0K, up 49,623 on the reference period), ahead of Direct (37.9K) and Referral (11.9K); Social fell by 15,669 sessions, and Display (21 sessions) is negligible. Organic Search sessions peaked at 12,732 in August 2019, 10,695 in July and 8,691 in June; Direct peaked at 7,902 in April 2019.
- Referral visitors are the most engaged: 111.5 seconds per session, 2.1 unique pageviews and 36.9 seconds on page, with monthly highs of 2.5 pageviews in October 2018 and 45 seconds on page in February 2019; Display is the least engaged at 9.8 seconds per session (208 seconds below its reference of 218), 1.0 unique pageview and 7.9 seconds on page.
- Among referral sources, google.com.br (91,833 sessions), indiegogo.com (48,792), cnet.com (11,346) and amazon.co.jp (10,872) bring the most sessions; ask.com, biblegateway.com and canalblog.com have the highest bounce (0.50) and exit rates (ask.com 50% this month), while timesonline.co.uk, cnbc.com and 4shared.com bounce least.

Sessions, Bar - Sessions
Total sessions 30.1K, up 69.8% year to date; the monthly trend climbs steadily from the lows of 372 in May 2017 and 1,056 in June 2017.

Sessions Durations, Bar - Sessions duration
Average session duration 67 seconds, up 36.2%; May 2017 was the high at 116 seconds and October 2017 the low at 19 seconds, with July (37 s) and December 2017 (38 s) also low.

bounce %, Bar - bounce %
Bounce rate 21%, down 11.8%; the lowest months are February, March, May and July 2019 at 19% and June 2019 at 20%.

Total Unique pageview, Bar - unique pageviews
Page views 50.7K, up 117.6%; unique pageviews per session were lowest in October 2017 (0.8), July 2017 (1.0), December 2017 (1.1) and August and November 2017 (1.2).

Avg Time on Page, Bar - avg time on page
Average time on page 30 seconds, up 3.2%; the low was October 2017 (20 s) and the high May 2017 (35 s).

Avg Page exits, Bar - page load time
Page exits 15%, down 24.3%; October 2017 (37%), July 2017 (24%) and December 2017 (23%) were the high months and May 2017 (10%) the low.

Sheet 70
Bounce % against page exits % by referral source: most sources sit at 10 to 20% exits and 15 to 25% bounce, and the two move together; google.com.br (91,833 sessions), indiegogo.com (48,792), cnet.com (11,346) and amazon.co.jp (10,872) are the largest sources, and ask.com, biblegateway.com and canalblog.com the highest bouncing.

Top Dim - Total Sessions - Perf Card, Top Dim - Total Sessions - Mini Trend
Sessions by channel: Organic Search 67.0K (66,960, up 49,623), Direct 37.9K, Referral 11.9K, Paid Search 10.3K, Social 10.2K (down 15,669) and Display 21; Organic Search, Direct, Referral and Paid Search are rising while Social and Display fall, with Organic Search at 12,732 in August 2019.

Top Dim - Session Duration - Perf Card, Top Dim - Mini Trends (Session Duration) (line chart)
Session duration by channel: Referral 111.5 seconds, Organic Search 84.3, Social 52.2, Paid Search 48.7, Direct 47.2 and Display 9.8, which is 208 seconds below its 218-second reference.

Top Dim - Avg Unique Pageviews - Perf Card, Top Dim - Mini Trends (Avg Unique Pageviews) (bar chart)
Unique pageviews per session by channel: Referral 2.1, Organic Search 1.9, Paid Search 1.5, Social and Direct 1.3 and Display 1.0 (1.1 below its reference of 2.1); Referral peaked at 2.5 in October 2018 and 2.4 in February and March 2019, Display sat at 0.7 in February and March 2019.

Top Dim - Avg Time on Page - Perf Card, Top Dim - Mini Trends (Avg Time on Page) (line chart)
Time on page by channel: Referral 36.9 seconds, Organic Search 31.4, Social 29.8, Direct 27.4, Paid Search 23.4 and Display 7.9 (44 seconds below its 52-second reference); Referral peaked at 45 seconds in February 2019 and 43 in March 2019, Paid Search at 44 seconds in November 2018.

expected.insightNarrative:
main page is the city factsheet of the Urban Audit city factsheets for 2019 Urban Adaptation Map Viewer, published by the European Environment Agency. A city is selected at the top; the dashboard shows Burgos, Spain, population 177,776, for the year 2014. The factsheet covers the city's observed and projected climate, its land cover and exposure to hazards, its socio-economic vulnerability and its adaptation activities, and lists the documents the figures come from. The story is a city with average heat and flood exposure, a rising forest fire danger and heavier summer downpours ahead, and no adaptation plan.

Key insights
- Flood exposure is stable: about 12% of all land uses are potentially exposed to a 1-in-100-year river flood, 12.35% in the 1961-1990 baseline and 11.92% projected for 2071-2100.
- The climate indicators with the highest values are 47.33 cooling degree days per year and a projected 22.41% increase in heavy summer precipitation by 2071-2100; forest fire danger is well above the average of other Urban Audit cities, and winter precipitation has fallen by 3.28 mm per decade.
- Burgos has no adaptation plan and has not signed the Covenant of Mayors on adaptation.
